- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for the next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates prices after a recent spike (e.g., >70) — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for 5–7 days post-spike.  
- Model overestimates early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral — reduce first 3–5 forecast points by 0.5–1.5%.  
- If sentiment shows a sharp reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33), model lags in adjusting — delay forecast correction by 1–2 days and apply gradual mean reversion.  
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above 70, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until price stabilizes.  
- For sentiment history with high volatility (alternating +/–0.33), model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth 3–5 day moving average before forecasting.
